evaluation_diagnostics.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A higher score requires a named clinic and qualified clinical team under costed responsibility terms, a documented protocol-specific regulatory route, at least two noncompeting sponsors signing and paying deposits for the same endpoint, legal confirmation of the proposed derived-benchmark reuse rights, a quoted cohort budget showing attractive contribution margin and cash timing, and evidence of repeat or renewal demand after the first protocol.
evaluation_diagnostics.highest_value_structural_change: Replace the initial two-sponsor consortium dependency with a clinic- or CRO-channel partnership and one anchor sponsor that fully funds a private, fixed-endpoint pilot under explicit permitted aggregate-data terms; add a second sponsor and shared benchmark product only after the protocol, economics, rights, and buyer utility have been demonstrated. This preserves the potential data asset while reducing simultaneous launch dependencies and borrowing clinical trust and operations.
evaluation_diagnostics.main_structural_strength: The opportunity converts a speculative cohort into a conditional, sponsor-precommitted protocol: funding, clinical responsibility, regulatory route, and lawful reuse rights must all be documented before major capital or participant exposure, while repeat standardized work could eventually create a compounding benchmark asset.
evaluation_diagnostics.primary_score_limiter: The commercial engine is an unproven multi-party coordination sale: the business cannot launch unless multiple sponsors share an endpoint and timing, prepay enough to cover external costs, a clinic accepts regulated responsibilities, and contracts permit useful pooled derivatives, all while established providers offer credible alternatives.
evaluation_diagnostics.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: VivoSense, Empatica, TNO, and Delve already market overlapping end-to-end wearable-study, device-integration, validation, regulatory, quality-control, and participant-operation capabilities, directly weakening the claim that this consortium has a sufficiently distinct or dominant offer; the packet provides no buyer evidence of an unmet Central-European gap to offset that competition.

evaluation_diagnostics.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A costed protocol and signed clinic/PI responsibility allocation; written protocol-specific regulatory and data-rights opinions; and, most importantly, at least two noncompeting sponsors signing deposits that cover external cohort costs at a demonstrated price, followed by evidence of usable-signal yield, gross margin, repeat demand, and lawful benchmark reuse.
evaluation_diagnostics.highest_value_structural_change: Remove the need for two sponsors to synchronize before the first sale: structure an anchor-sponsored fixed protocol in which one sponsor fully funds its validation, receives sponsor-specific outputs, and contractually permits only defined nonconfidential derived metrics to seed a reusable benchmark; add later sponsors asynchronously under the same protocol, with no launch unless the anchor price covers external costs.
evaluation_diagnostics.main_structural_strength: The model converts its largest uncertainties into explicit pre-launch gates: no participant operations or material cohort spending occurs until sponsors fund the study, qualified clinic roles accept responsibility, the regulatory route is documented, and benchmark rights are contractually bounded.
evaluation_diagnostics.primary_score_limiter: The business requires simultaneous sponsor, clinic, regulatory, and data-rights commitments, yet there is no evidence that sponsors will coordinate on one endpoint or prepay at economics that leave attractive recurring margins.
evaluation_diagnostics.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Established providers already market overlapping wearable protocol, analytics, clinical validation, regulatory, quality-control, and participant-operation capabilities, while no sponsor has evidenced a perceived Central-European consortium gap or accepted its price and shared-benchmark terms.

evaluation_diagnostics.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid pilots in one named vertical showing recurring difficult-case volume, quantified avoided losses, annual-contract willingness to pay, renewal intent, repeatable conversion and sales cycle, CAC payback, expert hours and contribution margin, superiority over incumbent alternatives, and explicit permission to reuse de-identified outcomes.
evaluation_diagnostics.highest_value_structural_change: Make the product the vertical system of record for SKU fact intake and classification-change monitoring, with qualified expert review reserved for escalations under a fixed-cost service layer; recurring workflow embedding would reduce dependence on sporadic BTI cases and create clearer switching costs.
evaluation_diagnostics.main_structural_strength: The design owns the importer renewal relationship and concentrates on a narrow, confidential, expert-backed exception workflow rather than competing as another generic HS-code predictor.
evaluation_diagnostics.primary_score_limiter: There is no evidence that any specific vertical combines sufficient recurring difficult-case density, annual willingness to pay, affordable acquisition, and scalable expert delivery; that single unproven dependency constrains the market, economics, and repeatability of the model.
evaluation_diagnostics.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Polish WIT filing and decisions are free, official tariff and ruling research is broadly public, and multiple incumbents already provide overlapping AI, bulk, API, reasoned-classification, and human-expert services, sharply limiting scarcity and differentiation.

evaluation_diagnostics.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Name one vertical and show a paid annual pilot with repeated difficult-SKU cases, quantified customer loss avoided, renewal intent, and a demonstrable advantage over incumbent managed services; also show actual expert hours and cost, gross margin, direct-sales CAC and payback, enforceable professional-liability terms, and either explicit reusable-data rights or a defensibility mechanism that does not depend on them.
evaluation_diagnostics.highest_value_structural_change: Make the product an embedded product-information and classification control layer at the mandatory new-SKU release gate for one chosen vertical, with structured fact completion on every SKU and qualified experts reviewing only flagged exceptions. That would create recurring workflow ownership, case density, switching costs, and scalable delivery without making optional reuse of confidential outcomes the sole compounding asset.
evaluation_diagnostics.main_structural_strength: The design focuses on the non-commodity portion of classification work and owns the direct importer renewal relationship, allowing a vertical workflow and expert exception layer to become valuable if repeat case density is established.
evaluation_diagnostics.primary_score_limiter: The opportunity has no identified, sized, or paid beachhead proving that recurring difficult-classification pain is dense enough to support annual contracts, scalable expert economics, and repeatable direct acquisition.
evaluation_diagnostics.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Mature providers already market automated classification, official-source reasoning, bulk processing, APIs, and human-expert review, while official Polish WIT filing is free and core rulings and tariff research are public; the proposed paid workflow therefore lacks a demonstrated behavior-changing advantage.

unresolved_evidence: A costed protocol and signed clinic/PI responsibility allocation; written protocol-specific regulatory and data-rights opinions; and, most importantly, at least two noncompeting sponsors signing deposits that cover external cohort costs at a demonstrated price, followed by evidence of usable-signal yield, gross margin, repeat demand, and lawful benchmark reuse.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A costed protocol and written regulatory route; signed clinic and qualified-role terms; at least two independent sponsors committing deposits around the same endpoint; counsel-validated participant, clinic, and sponsor terms permitting the proposed derived benchmark; and a pilot model showing price, gross margin, acquisition effort, delivery time, renewal intent, and a credible founder-net-worth path.
records.primary_score_limiter: The commercial engine depends on synchronizing at least two sponsors, qualified clinic roles, a protocol-specific regulatory route, and cross-sponsor derived-data rights before any delivery, without an existing channel or demonstrated advantage over established wearable CROs.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: VivoSense, Empatica, TNO, and Delve already market substantial portions of the proposed end-to-end wearable validation stack, directly weakening the claim that this entrant has a sufficiently differentiated or uncontested beachhead.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: For one named vertical: importer records showing recurring difficult-case frequency and avoidable loss; multiple paid annual pilots with observed conversion and sales cycle; repeat use or renewal; measured expert hours, contribution margin, liability and support cost, CAC and payback; signed permission for the intended de-identified reuse; and benchmarked accuracy, turnaround, or risk reduction versus incumbent tools and current advisers.
records.primary_score_limiter: The business has no evidence-selected beachhead or demonstrated control point beyond a direct contract: the same unknown vertical must supply sufficient complex-case density, paid annual demand, affordable acquisition, data-use rights, and repeatable expert margins despite mature overlapping incumbents.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Avalara already combines automated and managed classification, APIs, post-audit support, human experts, and large-catalogue scale, while eClear and TariffPilot provide further overlapping AI and reasoning workflows; this directly challenges the proposed offer's differentiation and domination potential.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Obtain an anchor-quality-and-operations commitment that specifies a real lane, baseline turn volume and current cost, acceptable price, minimum volume, qualification path, liability terms, and switching reason; pair it with written courier, lessor, cleaning, calibration, repair, insurance, and data-processing terms. A paid pilot should then measure utilization, cycle time, loss and damage, all-in contribution per turn, exception workload, audit performance, renewal intent, and founder hours against an incumbent or single-use baseline.
records.primary_score_limiter: The offer lacks a demonstrated buyer-side advantage or defensible control point against scaled full-stack incumbents, while its economics require the same uncommitted anchor, courier, lessor, and service partners to cooperate on favorable terms.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Established vendors already bundle reusable asset rental, reverse logistics, inspection and refurbishment, telemetry, alerts, reports, route tools, and analytics; the cited Swiss Post deployment also used roughly 8,000 boxes and nearby service-center operations, indicating that density and operating scale—not merely reporting software—are central to performance.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: For one named vertical and test family: paid annual or multi-cycle pilots showing incremental willingness to pay, observed testing frequency and deadline failures, collected subscription contribution after specialist and exception costs, acquisition conversion and CAC by channel, repeat or renewal behavior, founder operating hours, and written laboratory acceptance of the exact ordering, custody, name-use, service-level, and liability model.
records.primary_score_limiter: The proposed beachhead is not actually selected: one still-unknown test family must simultaneously have frequent urgent pain, incremental subscription willingness to pay, reachable buyers, cooperative laboratories, and enough contribution after specialist and liability costs.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: PORT, Hamilton, and TUV Rheinland already provide direct technical scoping, quotations, ordering, sampling or transport, and reporting, while Science Exchange and Scientist.com demonstrate mature orchestration platforms; this materially challenges whether the added calendar-and-custody layer is sufficiently better or independently valuable.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Obtain a legal-perimeter memo and then a live commercial-building pilot with at least two lenders on written, preferably non-exclusive terms disclosing commissions and data rights; measure eligible quote volume, abandonment, approval and funding conversion by lender, time-to-fund, installer activation and retention, CAC, integration and exception-support cost, gross margin, and whether multi-lender routing materially outperforms a tied-lender baseline.
records.primary_score_limiter: There is no evidenced economic or distribution wedge against scaled embedded-finance incumbents: neutral lender participation, commissions, commercial-project volume, installer adoption, conversion lift, support cost, exclusivity, and reusable outcome-data rights are all unresolved.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Inbank reports more than 200 Polish OZE partners and more than 80,000 prior green-installation loans, while Credit Agricole and BNP already embed fast credit in installer or merchant flows and Energa with SGB bundle technical delivery and financing; together this directly contradicts an open-channel or weak-incumbent thesis.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A paid or sponsor-prepaid pilot for one sharply defined protocol, paired with a costed clinic agreement that assigns qualified responsibilities and grants durable lawful rights to reuse derived benchmarks, plus comparative proof of a material price, speed, cohort-access, or validation-quality advantage and evidence of repeat sponsor demand.
records.primary_score_limiter: The business has not established an asymmetric control point or measurable buying advantage over mature wearable-CRO competitors; its intended moat depends simultaneously on clinic exclusivity and reusable benchmark rights that are both unproven.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: VivoSense, Empatica, TNO, and Delve already market overlapping end-to-end protocol, device, analytics, clinical-validation, quality-control, regulatory, and participant-operation capabilities, directly weakening the premise that the proposed integrated service is an underserved wedge.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid pilots with several capability-poor forwarders or importers showing monthly difficult-case volume, conversion at the proposed case price, actual specialist and liability costs, contribution margin and cash collection, workspace renewal, decision-quality or time savings versus incumbents, and signed permission to reuse de-identified outcomes; a scoped legal and insurance opinion on the operating model is also needed.
records.primary_score_limiter: The proposed control point is not owned: forwarders are expected to provide distribution and case data while some can deliver the service themselves, and no channel agreement, exclusive niche, or contractual outcome-data right currently prevents substitution.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Mature vendors already combine tariff automation, APIs, bulk workflow, reasoned outputs, and human expertise, while Maersk already sells HS-classification consulting through the intended channel; this directly challenges both differentiation and the forwarder-embedded acquisition thesis.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: The highest-value evidence would be a paid or binding minimum-volume pilot on a defined closed-loop lane, with buyer quality approval of the shared asset and data-rights model, contracted courier and service terms, and measured per-turn utilization, return time, loss, damage, cleaning, calibration, connectivity, exception, CAC, and willingness-to-pay data sufficient to demonstrate contribution margin and fleet payback under conservative volume.
records.primary_score_limiter: The candidate has no evidence-backed wedge against scaled full-stack incumbents that already provide the same rental, reverse-logistics, telemetry, reporting, and analytics bundle, leaving acquisition, density, and pricing power structurally weak.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Multiple established vendors already sell the proposed feature bundle, and the disclosed Swiss Post deployment relied on roughly 8000 boxes plus nearby cleaning, inspection, and repair capacity, directly challenging the premise that a small Warsaw pilot can quickly achieve differentiated network economics.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: For one narrowly defined test family, obtain a laboratory term sheet covering authorized resale, name use, current method scope, SLA or reservable capacity, cancellation, liability, and net pricing; then show paid SME pilots with invoice-level contribution margin, measurable turnaround improvement, quote-to-order conversion, acquisition cost, repeat behavior, and willingness to pay the spread.
records.primary_score_limiter: The proposal has not identified a narrow segment where buyers experience enough unresolved procurement or turnaround pain to pay an intermediary while laboratories grant usable reservation and resale terms at economics that survive direct-provider competition.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: PORT, Hamilton, and TUV Rheinland already offer direct ordering, technical scoping, quotations, sampling or transport, and reports, while Science Exchange and Scientist.com already provide mature procurement orchestration; this materially challenges the claim that the proposed layer is sufficiently better or structurally scarce.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A paid, end-to-end pilot with an authorized registry partner and several multi-site accounts showing recurring hard exceptions, documented baseline versus product time and error reduction, claim-safe accepted outputs, actual onboarding and usage prices, partner take rate, gross margin after exception labor, acquisition cost, payback, renewal intent, and a credible volume path that does not require a large share of the Polish market.
records.primary_score_limiter: The necessary registry and distribution partners already control the customer and can perform or copy much of the workflow, leaving the operator without a proven advantage, protected control point, or demonstrated margin capture.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: TGE added bulk transactions and a marketplace in April 2026, while Ecohz, Soldera, and Energy Solution already offer procurement, allocation, cancellation, status monitoring, proof storage, or Polish TGE certificate delivery; this directly contradicts a broad orchestration-gap thesis.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A live UPS Poland cohort should quantify guaranteed-service share, exclusion-adjusted late incidence, mean net credit, submission success and denial rates, labor minutes per attempt and credit, time to cash, and realized take rate across enough parcels to calculate contribution margin. A signed WMS or 3PL pilot, documented account-owner authorization, a repeatable acquisition cost, and evidence that customers prefer the localized workflow over incumbents would materially raise confidence.
records.primary_score_limiter: The recoverable revenue pool and operating leverage are both unproven: the product needs enough guaranteed parcels, eligible late events, credit value, and automated claim throughput while facing established broader competitors and carrier-controlled permissions.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: LateShipment.com and Refund Retriever already commercialize automated eligibility, claim filing, and verified-credit recovery at published contingency rates, with broader carrier or invoice-error coverage; generic late-parcel detection plus success pricing therefore supplies neither differentiation nor a credible domination path.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A named vertical with demonstrably unique fulfillment or usage evidence; a matched-cohort pilot showing incremental net recovery after all dispute, countering, channel, analyst, and success fees versus native PSP and specialist tools; written partner authorization for submission and final-outcome access; merchant demand and dispute-volume data; and a costed GDPR, PCI DSS, security, CAC, payback, gross-margin, and founder-time model.
records.primary_score_limiter: The candidate has not identified or secured the proprietary vertical evidence and partner access needed to outperform incumbents that already control submission rails, merchant transaction data, broad integrations, and success-priced automation.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Visa already controls major pre-dispute and evidence-routing infrastructure; Stripe and Adyen control programmatic dispute rails; Stripe, Chargeflow, and Justt already sell closely overlapping automation on outcome-based terms; and Visa's same-merchant CE3.0 requirement prevents other cooperative members' transactions from supplying the proposed direct evidence advantage.
